instructions.question: What overall feeling does the tweet's author show toward its topic: positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Positive includes mild warmth: excitement about a plan, friendly invitations ('see you there!'), good-luck wishes, excited fan outbursts, holiday fun, tributes to the dead, and news of wins, releases or new products. Neutral is dry information, plain or hedged plans and activities, logistics, ads, ticket sales, questions, speculation and calm analysis. Negative needs explicit annoyance, insults, disappointment, worry, personal setbacks, or harmful news like deaths, attacks or protests. Hypothetical sadness, self-mocking stress and ironic exaggeration stay neutral.

neutral.what: Factual updates, plain plans and activity reports, logistics, ads, questions, predictions, and opinions without emotional words.
examples: Going to see Paper Towns on Saturday. I'm hoping it does the book justice.
Pochettino should have started Alli. He'll probably do a Kane and keep him on the bench till November. Might be too late for him this term
when I go to the Foo Fighters concert in October in Atlanta I'm gonna be so sad if don't get to meet Dave Grohl somehow
neutral.cues: going to, tickets, specials, ?, should have, may, probably, hoping, if
neutral.not_for: Plans or invitations with clear enthusiasm (positive); explicit complaints, insults, or harm (negative).

positive.what: Warmth, excitement, praise, well-wishing or tribute, or good news such as wins, releases and launches.
examples: It’s Tuesday night in Athens! AKA karaoke night at the Volstead so come see me!!
Guess who's going to see Foo Fighters on Tuesday!!!!! (ME)
New iPhones, iPad Pro, and Apple TV on the way today at 10 A.M. (PDT)! #AppleEvent
Happy Birthday Wilt Chamberlain may you rest in peace
positive.cues: see you, come see, good luck, can't wait, love, best, awesome, happy, tribute, wins, flailing, OMG, :)
positive.not_for: Flat or doubtful plans, dry schedules, ads or listings (neutral); sarcastic 'can't wait' (negative).

negative.what: Anger, sadness, worry, insults, personal disappointment or inconvenience, and news of deaths, attacks, losses or protests.
examples: It sucks we live in a world where Sharknado is about to start a 4th sequel but we can't get a Tron 3 or Dredd 2.
@user so the thing next Thursday isn't free, you'd have to pay $15 to get in since you don't go to UMBC :/ and it ends at 11:30"
negative.cues: sucks, wtf, hate, pity, nervous, ugh, #fml, crying, :/, :(, killed, delayed, boo, protest
negative.not_for: Calm arguments, hedged speculation, playful exaggeration, or RIP tributes (neutral or positive).
